title: Redeemed from curse; made God’s righteousness in him
source_text: XVIII. Eodem quoque spectat quod dicit idem Apostolus Christum nos redemisse ab execratione legis, dum factus est pro nobis ipse execratio: Gal. 3. Deum fecisse peccatum eum qui non noverat peccatum, ut nos efficeremur justitia Dei in ipso: 2 Cor. 5. 21. Christum a Deo nobis factum fuisse sapientiam, justitiam, sanctificationem & redemptionem: 1 Cor. 1. 30. Et sicut per unius hominis inobedientiam peccatores constituti sunt multi, ita per unius obedientiam multos esse constituendos justos: Rom. 5. 19.
pass_a_gloss: To the same point also tends what the same Apostle says: that Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, himself becoming a curse for us (Gal. 3); that God made him who knew no sin to be sin, that we might become the righteousness of God in him (2 Cor. 5:21); that Christ was made for us by God wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption (1 Cor. 1:30); and that just as by one man’s disobedience many were constituted sinners, so by one man’s obedience many are to be constituted righteous (Rom. 5:19).
pass_b_english: Christ became a curse; God made him sin that we become God’s righteousness in him.
He is our wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, redemption; one obedience constitutes many just.
